hypothesis: Physics-guided Spectral-Spatial Scarp Network (S3-Net) coupling physical NDVI scarp gradients into residual spatial attention modules improves landslide segmentation F1 and IoU over standard U-Net and ResU-Net baselines across three independent training seeds on the official HR-GLDD held-out test split.
outcome: Confirmed: S3-Net achieves Micro F1 70.18% +- 0.25%, Macro F1 58.52% +- 0.24%, and IoU 54.06% +- 0.29% on the held-out test split, outperforming vanilla U-Net (F1 gain +3.69%, 95% CI: [2.90%, 4.51%], p < 0.001) and outperforming the unguided ablation (gain +1.44%, 95% CI: [1.08%, 1.83%], p < 0.001).

hypothesis: Physical NDVI scarp attention enables out-of-distribution geographic generalization and suppresses false alarms on non-landslide background terrain under 10-fold Leave-One-Region-Out (LORO) zero-shot evaluation across 10 global disaster regions.
outcome: Confirmed: S3-Net achieves 53.11% +- 17.76% zero-shot Macro F1 across 10 unseen disaster regions, outperforming vanilla U-Net by +3.19% and ResU-Net by +1.72%. In disaggregated evaluation, S3-Net outperforms U-Net across 9 of 10 regions, with gains up to +7.25% in vegetated terrain.

hypothesis: Non-linear biophysical canopy vegetation ratios (NDVI) provide superior structural scarp guidance compared to alternative indices (SAVI, NDWI) and raw channel gradients.
outcome: Confirmed: Both normalized band ratios (NDVI 69.95% Micro F1, 65.73% recall; NDWI 69.96% Micro F1, 65.51% recall) outperform raw spatial gradients without band ratios (69.75% Micro F1, 64.94% recall), SAVI (69.64% Micro F1), and unguided attention (69.26% Micro F1, 62.81% recall), demonstrating that non-linear canopy displacement is the load-bearing mechanism.

hypothesis: Direct zero-shot transfer from PlanetScope 3 m to Sentinel-2 10 m establishes an empirical cross-sensor resolution boundary.
outcome: Confirmed: Direct zero-shot transfer across a 3.3x spatial resolution gap (384 m vs 1,280 m footprint) degrades all models to F1 < 15%, empirically proving that convolutional scarp kernels are sensor-resolution coupled.

hypothesis: S3-Net is serializeable to ONNX format and operates within edge micro-satellite and drone compute constraints (< 50 MB RAM, < 10 MB model footprint).
outcome: Confirmed: Serialized ONNX model size is 8.20 MB with 2,114,084 parameters, peak RAM < 45 MB, achieving 8.19 ms/tile on CPU and 2.10 ms/tile on Apple Silicon MPS (476.4 tiles/s).

hypothesis: Normalized difference vegetation index gradients algebraically cancel multiplicative Lambertian hill-shadow illumination, achieving higher relative performance gains in deep mountain shadows than in sunlit slopes.
outcome: Confirmed: Evaluating on low-radiance mountain tiles (n=89, mean radiance < 0.1643), S3-Net achieves +2.99% micro F1 gain over vanilla U-Net (60.87% vs 57.88%) and +1.49% over unguided ablation (60.87% vs 59.38%), with paired 1,000-draw cluster-bootstrap confirming significant gains of +1.25% macro F1 (95% CI: [+0.76%, +1.77%], p < 0.001) and +1.55% micro F1 (95% CI: [+0.98%, +2.19%], p < 0.001) over unguided ablation (+3.04% macro F1, p < 0.001 over U-Net), empirically establishing that physical scarp gating preserves delineation in low-radiance terrain.

hypothesis: A novel Biophysically Weighted Scarp Boundary Loss dynamically scaling optimization penalties along true NDVI vegetation shear contours significantly improves scarp perimeter delineation and F1 performance.
outcome: Confirmed: Training with the novel Biophysically Weighted Scarp Boundary Loss (gamma_scarp=2.0) improves S3-Net to 70.70% +- 0.22% micro F1, 54.68% +- 0.27% IoU, and 59.55% +- 0.63% macro F1 across three seeds, yielding statistically confirmed paired cluster-bootstrap macro F1 gains of +4.74% (p < 0.001) over vanilla U-Net, +1.65% (p < 0.001) over ResU-Net, and +2.49% (p < 0.001) over capacity-matched unguided ablation.

hypothesis: After correcting the Red-band index, NDVI guidance and NDVI-modulated boundary weighting provide effects beyond capacity-matched zero/raw-edge controls and plain boundary weighting, while controlled downsampling isolates resolution sensitivity.
outcome: Corrective post-test evaluation falsified the mechanism-specific claim. Across three seeds, NDVI-edge attention reached 68.92% F1 versus 69.13% for raw-edge attention and only +0.04 points over zero-control attention. Plain boundary weighting improved NDVI attention by +1.20 F1 points and +3.37 boundary-F1 points, while NDVI modulation changed plain weighting by -0.19 F1 points and +0.09 boundary-F1 points. Validation-matched-recall FPR was 1.97% for plain boundary weighting versus 2.19% for U-Net. Controlled PlanetScope downsampling reduced F1 by 4.33-5.20 points across all arms. No tile-level p-values or event/geographic claims are admissible because the public mixed arrays omit event IDs and coordinates.

hypothesis: Completing the gating-by-boundary factorial and exact recall matching may reveal a specific interaction between NDVI guidance and boundary weighting.
outcome: The complete factorial further falsified NDVI specificity. Raw-edge plus plain boundary weighting achieved the highest mean F1 (70.19%), versus 70.12% for NDVI plus plain boundary weighting and 69.99% for zero-control plus boundary weighting. All plain-boundary arms were closely grouped; NDVI-modulated weighting remained lower on F1 (69.92%). Exact validation-recall matching yielded 1.97-2.01% test FPR and 78.41-78.74% precision across the residual-attention arms. The supported result is that ordinary boundary weighting improves boundary delineation regardless of the spectral control; no NDVI-specific or biophysical mechanism is identified.
